He previously played for the [[NBA G League Ignite]]. ==Early life and high school career== Leonard Miller was born in [[Scarborough, Toronto|Scarborough]], [[Ontario]], and played basketball, [[volleyball]] and [[golf]] during his childhood.{{cite web |title=Leonard Miller |url=https://www.prospectiveinsight.com/post/leonard-miller |publisher=Pro Insight |access-date=June 11, 2022 |date=November 23, 2021}} He played basketball for [[Bill Crothers Secondary School]] in [[Markham, Ontario]], for grade 9 from 2017 to 2018{{Cite web |date=2023-02-10 |title=Canada’s Miller continues carving out name with G League Ignite as eyes set on NBA |url=https://rdnewsnow.com/2023/02/10/canadas-miller-continues-carving-out-name-with-g-league-ignite-as-eyes-set-on-nba/ |access-date=2025-06-18 |website=rdnewsnow.com |language=en}} and transferred to [[Thornlea Secondary School]] in [[Thornhill, Ontario]], for grade 10, where he helped the team win the National Junior Circuit title in March 2019.{{cite web |last=Mikre |first=Mickias |title=National Jr. Circuit Championships Recap – Thornlea crowned as 2019 Champions |url=https://northpolehoops.com/2019/03/06/national-jr-circuit-championships-recap-thornlea-crowned-as-2019-champions/ |publisher=North Pole Hoops |access-date=June 11, 2022 |date=March 6, 2019}} Miller transferred to [[Wasatch Academy]] in [[Mount Pleasant, Utah]], to face stronger competition but received limiting playing time. He transferred to Victory Rock Prep in [[Bradenton, Florida]], before missing several months with a broken right wrist in November 2020 that required surgery.{{cite web |last=Osman |first=Libaan |title=How Scarborough’s Leonard Miller became this year’s most intriguing NBA draft prospect |url=https://www.thestar.com/news/gta/2022/05/27/how-scarboroughs-leonard-miller-became-this-years-most-intriguing-nba-draft-prospect.html |website=[[Toronto Star]] |access-date=June 11, 2022 |date=May 27, 2022}} Miller opted to play a [[postgraduate year|postgraduate]] season at Fort Erie International Academy in [[Fort Erie, Ontario]] after growing 6' 4" guard to 6' 10" guard/wing over an 18-month period, and had no college offers at the time he made the decision.{{cite web |last=Kalbrosky |first=Bryan |title=Leonard Miller is suddenly the most intriguing NBA draft prospect, but it's what he does next that matters most |url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2022/05/nba-draft-leonard-miller-kentucky-arizona-g-league-ignite-overtime-elite |publisher=For The Win |access-date=June 11, 2022 |date=May 6, 2022}} He became the team's star player and received over 25 offers from college programs. Miller led Fort Erie to an Ontario Scholastic Basketball Association title and was named league [[most valuable player]]. He was selected to play for the World Team in the [[Nike Hoop Summit]].{{cite web |last=Pilgrim |first=Jack |title=Leonard Miller among top participants at Nike Hoop Summit |url=https://www.on3.com/teams/kentucky-wildcats/news/leonard-miller-among-top-participants-at-nike-hoop-summit/ |publisher=On3 |access-date=June 11, 2022 |date=April 6, 2022}} On April 23, 2022, he declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]].{{cite web |last=Backus |first=Will |title=Leonard Miller, uncommitted prospect in 2022 class, declares for NBA Draft |url=https://247sports.com/Article/Leonard-Miller-uncommitted-prospect-in-2022-class-declares-for-NBA-Draft-186654105/ |publisher=[[247Sports]] |access-date=June 11, 2022 |date=April 23, 2022}} On June 13, 2022, he withdrew from the draft and decided to play with the [[NBA G League Ignite]] for the next season.{{Cite web |last=Givony |first=Johnathan |date=2022-06-13 |title=Miller opts for G League Ignite instead of draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/34084656 |access-date=2024-06-15 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} ===Recruiting=== Miller was considered a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] and was ranked as the 2nd ranked prospect by [[On3.com]] despite playing in Canada with On3 ranking him first with the highest upside in the recruiting class.{{Cite web |title=Leonard Miller - Recruiting Profile |url=https://www.on3.com/db/leonard-miller-150920/recruiting/ |access-date=2024-06-15 |website=on3.com}} On May 31, 2022, he announced that he would pursue professional options instead of playing [[college basketball]].{{cite web |last=Siegel |first=Brett |title=Potential First-Round Pick Leonard Miller To Skip College, Play Professionally |url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/draft/potential-2022-nba-draft-pick-leonard-miller-to-skip-college-and-play-professionally |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=June 11, 2022 |date=May 31, 2022}} ==Professional career== ===NBA G League Ignite (2022–2023)=== On September 7, 2022, Miller signed a contract with the [[NBA G League Ignite]].{{cite web | last=Taylor | first=Cody | title=Mojave King, Leonard Miller officially sign contracts with G League Ignite | website=Rookie Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=2022-09-07 | url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/rookie/2022/09/07/nba-g-league-ignite-mojave-king-leonard-miller-contracts/77622397007/ | access-date=2025-12-03}} He was named to the G League's inaugural Next Up Game for the 2022–23 season.{{Cite web |date=February 8, 2023 |title=Wolves' Garza And Ignite's Henderson Named Captains For NBA G League Next Up Game |url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/wolves-garza-and-ignites-henderson-named-captains-for-nba-g-league-next-up-game |access-date=March 8, 2023 |website=NBA G League}} ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2023–2026)=== Miller was drafted in the second round of the [[2023 NBA draft]] with the 33rd overall pick by the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. He was then traded to the Minnesota Timberwolves on draft night. He made his summer league debut in Las Vegas on July 7, 2023.{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Schad|title=Leonard Miller, Josh Minott look like budding stars in Timberwolves' summer league opener|url=https://www.si.com/fannation/bringmethesports/timberwolves/leonard-miller-josh-minott-look-like-budding-stars-in-timberwolves-summer-league-opener|website=SI.com|date=July 8, 2023|access-date=July 9, 2023}} The Timberwolves announced they had signed Miller to a contract on July 9 of that year.{{cite web|title=Timberwolves Sign Leonard Miller|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-leonard-miller|website=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2023|access-date=July 9, 2023}} Miller made 17 appearances for Minnesota during his rookie campaign, posting averages of 1.7 points, 1.2 rebounds, and 0.5 assists.{{Cite web|title=Leonard Miller 2023–24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/5044385/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=February 11, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} Miller played in 13 games for the Timberwolves during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 1.5 points and 0.8 rebounds.{{Cite web|title=Leonard Miller 2024–25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/5044385/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=February 11, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} Throughout his rookie and sophomore seasons, he was [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] several times to the [[Iowa Wolves]].{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Iowa Wolves Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Iowa-Wolves/4/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 23, 2024}}{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Iowa Wolves Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Iowa-Wolves/4/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 23, 2024}} Miller made 19 appearances for Minnesota in the [[2025–26 NBA season]], logging averages of 2.3 points, 1.3 rebounds, and 0.3 assists.{{Cite web|title=Leonard Miller 2025–26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/5044385/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=February 11, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===Chicago Bulls (2026–present)=== On February 5, 2026, Miller, [[Rob Dillingham]], and four second-round picks were traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]] in exchange for [[Ayo Dosunmu]] and [[Julian Phillips (basketball)|Julian Philips]].{{Cite web |title=Bulls continue demolition of roster, trade Ayo Dosunmu and others |url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/bulls/2026/02/05/bulls-continue-demolition-trading-ayo-dosunmu-and-others |access-date=2026-02-05 |website=[[Chicago Sun-Times]] |language=en-US }}{{Cite web |title=Timberwolves acquire Ayo Dosunmu from Bulls in trade |url=https://www.nba.com/news/ayo-dosunumu-trade-wolves-bulls |access-date=2026-02-05 |website=[[NBA.com]] |language=en-US }} ==National team career== Miller won a silver medal with Canada at the [[2019 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship]] in Brazil, averaging
